problem: It says init-params and context-params are 'Both ... set in web.xml or annotations'. Init-params can be declared in an annotation (@WebInitParam inside @WebServlet), but there is no annotation for context-params. A student will look for an annotation that does not exist.
fix: Write: 'Init-params are set in web.xml or with @WebInitParam inside @WebServlet. Context-params have no annotation; set them in web.xml with <context-param>, or at startup in a ServletContextListener using getServletContext().setInitParameter().' Both reach your code as strings.

problem: 'The container, not your code, chooses the method' is misleading. The client (browser) sends the method; the container only dispatches on it. A student may read it as the container deciding GET or POST.
fix: 'The client sends the HTTP method in the request line. service() reads it and dispatches to the matching doXxx() method; your code never calls doGet() or doPost() itself.'

problem: 'For a form POST, Tomcat parses the body and getParameter still works' is true only for application/x-www-form-urlencoded forms. For multipart/form-data (file upload) getParameter returns null.
fix: 'For an application/x-www-form-urlencoded form POST, Tomcat parses the body and getParameter still works. For multipart/form-data, add @MultipartConfig or read parts with getPart().'

problem: The class is a plain Java class (GreetServletSim) with doGet(String, int), not a servlet. Nothing in the example says it is a simulation, so a student may copy this signature as the servlet doGet.
fix: State before the code: 'This small class simulates what the container does so you can see the call order. The real servlet extends HttpServlet and its doGet takes HttpServletRequest and HttpServletResponse, as shown in step 3.'

problem: The step uses res.setContentType("text/html") without a charset, while the chapter and the exam traps insist on setting the charset before getWriter(). The example contradicts its own rule.
getParameter returns null when the parameter is absent, and a non-numeric value also fails, so Integer.parseInt throws NumberFormatException. The chapter mentions parseInt but not this failure.
fix: Add: 'getParameter returns null if the parameter is missing, so check for null and catch NumberFormatException before using Integer.parseInt().'
